subject: human eye
title: Your Cornea Has No Blood Vessels. It Breathes Straight From the Air

scenes.text: One part of your body has no blood supply at all, and you're looking through it.
It's your cornea, the clear dome on the front of your eye.
Blood vessels would cloud it, so it has none.
Instead it takes oxygen straight from the air, dissolved in your tears.
Close your eyes to sleep and that supply drops, from about 21 percent oxygen to around 8.
So at night it borrows oxygen from blood vessels inside your eyelid. The window you see through breathes air.

description:
Your cornea has no blood vessels. It takes its oxygen directly from the air, dissolved in the tear film.
About half a millimetre thick, the cornea stays transparent because it is avascular. With your eyes open it draws on air at about 21 percent oxygen; when you sleep, it relies on the blood vessels of the inner eyelid and the oxygen available drops to about 7 or 8 percent.

first_comment: This is also why sleeping in contact lenses is risky: they cut the cornea's air supply even more. Did you know this one?
